Roles
EasyRole guide

Support

The team's guardian and vision master: protect, set up plays, and see everything.

You'll enjoy this role if…

  • You like helping teammates more than racking up kills.
  • You'd rather skip farming minions.
  • You enjoy setting up plays, saving allies and controlling vision.
  • You want to have a say in where the team goes.

What this role does

Supports play bot lane with the ADC but don't need minion gold. Instead, they protect their carry, start fights, place wards, and roam to help other lanes. A great support makes the whole team better.

  • Protect your ADC in lane and in fights.
  • Start fights (engage) or stop the enemy from starting them (disengage).
  • Place and clear wards: you control your team's vision.
  • Roam to help mid and the jungler when bot lane is safe.
  • Leave minions to your ADC: let them take the farm.

Support types

  • Engage supports like Leona, Nautilus and Thresh jump on enemies with stuns and hooks. They start fights and create kills.
  • Enchanters like Lulu, Soraka, Janna and Sona heal, shield and speed up their allies, keeping the carry alive.
  • Wardens like Braum protect allies by standing in front of them and blocking damage.
  • Mage supports like Lux and Morgana poke the enemy and catch them with crowd control.

Engage supports are best when your team wants to fight. Enchanters are best with a strong carry to protect.

Your support item and quest

Supports start with World Atlas, the support item. It gives you gold when you damage enemies or stay near your ADC, so you don't need to take minions.

The support role quest needs 800 points. Completing it upgrades your item from Runic Compass into Bounty of Worlds, which you can then upgrade for free into a final support item like Celestial Opposition, Solstice Sleigh, Dream Maker, Bloodsong or Zaz'Zak's Realmspike. Pick the one that fits your champion.

Supports also get cheaper Control Wards (40 gold instead of 75), and up to 2 Control Wards are stored in your quest slot from the start, so they don't take item space.

Common mistakeDon't take minion last hits when your ADC is nearby. Their gold matters much more than yours, and supports outside bot lane get 33% less minion gold and experience until level 5 anyway.

Early game in lane

  • Help win the level 2 race. Damage the first wave so you and your ADC hit level 2 before the enemy. Then go in together.
  • Poke and zone. Hit the enemy ADC when they walk up to last-hit. Standing forward in the lane can scare them away from minions.
  • Engage when the enemy makes a mistake: when they're out of position, low, or used their escape.
  • Protect your ADC from ganks. Ward the river and tri-brush around 2:30-3:00, when the enemy jungler might arrive.
Pro tipWatch the enemy support's key ability. If their hook or stun is on cooldown, your lane has a few seconds to fight with no risk.

Warding

Vision is one of the support's biggest jobs. With vision, your team sees ganks coming and fights with information.

  • Early on, ward the river and tri-brush near bot lane.
  • Before dragon spawns, ward around the dragon pit about a minute early.
  • Buy Control Wards every recall. They reveal and disable enemy wards.
  • Once your support item is upgraded, swap your trinket to Oracle Lens to clear enemy wards.
  • Use Faelights: a ward placed on one gets 25% more sight range.

Each player can have 3 Stealth Wards and 1 Control Ward placed at a time. Learn more in Vision Basics: Wards and the Minimap and Advanced Vision Control.

Roaming and the mid game

Once bot lane is safe (for example, your ADC just recalled), roam to mid or help your jungler with the Scuttler or an invade. A support showing up in mid lane often creates an easy kill.

In the mid game, walk with your carries and place vision ahead of them. Clear enemy wards around objectives with Oracle Lens. Don't let your carries walk into unwarded areas alone.

Read Roaming and Map Pressure to learn when to leave lane.

Late game and teamfights

  • Engage supports: look for a fight-starting engage on a key target, but only when your team is close enough to follow.
  • Enchanters: stay near your carry. Shield, heal and speed them up when they're attacked.
  • Everyone: keep your crowd control for the enemy divers and assassins who jump on your carry. This is called peeling.

A support who dies first in a fight often loses the fight. Don't facecheck brushes alone: use wards or sweep with your Oracle Lens first.

Beginner-friendly champions

LeonaTanky engage support with lots of stuns. Teaches you when to start fights.
SorakaSimple healer who keeps her whole team alive.
LuxLong-range poke and roots. Easy to play safely.
NautilusHook, stun and knock-ups. One of the easiest engage supports.
SonaSimple enchanter who heals, speeds up allies and has a team-wide stun ultimate.

Common mistakes

  • Taking minions from your ADC.
  • Not buying Control Wards or never using your trinket.
  • Engaging when your ADC isn't ready or can't follow.
  • Roaming while your ADC is alone in a dangerous lane.
  • Facechecking brushes alone in the late game.
  • Using your crowd control to start a fight instead of protecting your carry when they're getting dived.
